evidence.detail: R302 InterfaceRenderer iterates active rs/l/e/f feature controllers during live widget traversal, looks up rs/l/e/i by the current RSInterface.aw id, and invokes it with the concrete RSInterface plus the already-resolved screen x/y coordinates.

The controller base rs/l/e/f owns an int-keyed map of rs/l/e/i callbacks. Its protected registration helpers bind either one widget id or an int[] of widget ids to the same callback, and only controllers with non-empty callback maps enter the renderer-consumed callback list.

Concrete rs/l/e/a/* controller implementations instantiate rs/l/e/i callbacks for specific interface id sets; those callbacks inspect the supplied RSInterface and perform feature-specific presentation such as sprite drawing from widget state.

This contract is distinct from R288 InterfaceDrawCallback: R288 is stored directly on RSInterface and preserves draw(int,int), while rs/l/e/i is externally registered by active feature controllers and receives (RSInterface,int,int).

candidates.note: Descriptive exact-v308 name for the feature-controller callback invoked by InterfaceRenderer for a widget id with the concrete RSInterface and resolved coordinates; intentionally distinguished from R288 InterfaceDrawCallback.
